newsitem.title: USA: FDA stops use of dioxin-tainted livestock feed.
newsitem.headline: FDA stops use of dioxin-tainted livestock feed.

text.p: The Food and Drug Administration Thursday barred further sale and distribution of poultry feed that was tainted with dioxin, a dangerous chemical compound.

The FDA said the levels of dioxin found in the feed, and the foods produced by the chickens that ate the feed, presented no immediate public health hazard. The FDA blocked the feed "as a precautionary measure to reduce the potential human exposure to dioxin."

The source of the dioxin was traced to a single mine in Mississippi that produces a clay commonly used as an anti-caking agent in feed. Mining and shipping from that mine have been halted at the FDA's request.

A national sampling by the FDA and other agencies showed chickens at Tyson Foods Inc plants in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, and Seguin, Texas, had elevated dioxin levels. Tyson Foods last month said a feed supplier to those plants, Riceland Foods Inc of Stuttgart, Arkansas, had stopped using the clay agent in its feed.
Dioxins are environmentally persistent chemical compounds that are an unwanted byproduct of a number of industrial processes.
The compounds -- which are found at low levels throughout the environment and accumulate in the food chain -- may cause cancer, disrupt the endocrine system and cause other health disorders.
